interface.title: JALEBI — JWST Analysis of Line Emission with Bayesian Inference
interface.field: Infrared astronomy / protoplanetary-disk molecular spectroscopy (JWST MIRI-MRS)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis: continuum subtraction, molecular slab model fitting, Bayesian inference, IFU cube mapping and rotation diagrams
interface.what_it_is_for: Fitting LTE molecular slab models and rotation diagrams to JWST/MIRI disk spectra and mapping lines in IFU cubes, with grid → optimiser → MCMC inference.

data.note: The bundled FZ Tau MIRI x1d spectrum (12 sub-bands, 11637 px) was preloaded as the session source. The bundled HV Tau C cubes (5 s3d: 1A, 2B, 3A, 3A, 3C) were opened in Cube maps by typing example:HV_Tau_C_cube. A Scan on the Source page also lists synthetic CSV tables.

tree.general: Measure what molecules and gas conditions are present in a disk's infrared spectrum and where line emission sits on the sky
tree.specific: Fit LTE slab models to the FZ Tau MIRI spectrum, fit H2/CO rotation diagrams, and map [Ne II] in the HV Tau C cube

features.name: Baseline estimator with method switch and residual preview
features.general: Pick a baseline algorithm, tune its parameters, protect or mask ranges, and see the baseline-subtracted signal and per-segment noise update at once
features.specific: Continuum tab: choose a method (irsqr, median_sg, asls, aspls, convex_hull, rolling_min, spline, banzatti, sgclip, none, given). Its parameter boxes change with the method (quantile/knots, λ/p, hull segment/overlap). Protected Q-branch ranges and masks (H I/H2 lines, OH prompt lines, 9–13 µm) are optional. With auto-update on, the continuum-subtracted plot and the MAD-noise table per sub-band refresh.
steps: choose a method in the dropdown
adjust the method-specific parameters
toggle protected ranges or masks
read the continuum-subtracted plot, the noise table and the χ²_red chip
serves_tasks: Fit a baseline with one of several methods and compare the residuals

features.name: Live multi-component model with parameter sliders and residual panel
features.general: Build a sum of model components, each with sliders and number boxes, and watch the model overlay, the residuals and the goodness of fit update as you drag
features.specific: Components panel: add a slab (molecule, line list), tune log N / T / log R with sliders, toggle it on/off or remove it. The Model overlay, the Residual (data−model)/σ plot and the χ²_red chip update. Auto areas (NNLS) solves the emitting areas in one click.
steps: choose a molecule and press + add
drag the log N, T and log R sliders
press Auto areas (NNLS)
read the overlay, the residual plot and χ²_red
serves_tasks: Adjust model parameters by hand and watch the model and residuals update live
Add a second model component for another species and solve all component amplitudes at once

features.name: 2-D Δχ² grid map that sets the controls
features.general: Compute a goodness-of-fit heat map over two parameters for one component, mark the minimum, and push the best point back into the controls
features.specific: Grid map (log N, T): pick a component and press Compute grid. The log10(Δχ²+1) heat map shows a red cross at the best point and an optically-thin boundary line. The best log N, T and log R go to the sliders, with a toast.
steps: choose a component
press Compute grid (log N, T)
read the heat map and its best-point marker
continue from the updated sliders
serves_tasks: Map goodness of fit over a 2-D parameter grid and send the best point to the controls

features.name: Template detection table with significance threshold and add-to-model
features.general: Fit every candidate template at once, rank them by information-criterion gain against a threshold, then put the detected ones into the model
features.specific: Detect molecules: set the ΔBIC threshold and press Detect molecules (shows progress). The table lists candidate, T, log N, log R/f_c, Δχ², ΔBIC, local χ²_red, pixels and windows, with a ✓ for detections, plus suggested fit windows. Use detected components / Add missing only buttons are offered to send detections to the Components panel; they were not pressed in this run.
steps: set the ΔBIC threshold
press Detect molecules
read the ranked table and the suggested windows
(not yet exercised) press Use detected components or Add missing only
serves_tasks: Test which candidate species are significantly present

features.name: Staged fit runner with live log and convergence trace
features.general: Configure and run a pipeline of grid search, global optimiser and MCMC, with a progress bar, a stop button, a streaming log and a live chain log-probability plot
features.specific: Fit tab: toggle the grid/optimise/mcmc stages and set the grid ranges, the optimiser (de, maxiter, popsize) and MCMC walkers/steps/processes/seed. Run fit shows the stage name, percent and elapsed time, logs best −2lnP per generation, then plots mean ln p of the walkers (16–84% band).
steps: toggle the stages
set the grid, optimiser and MCMC settings
press Run fit (Stop to abort)
watch the log and the ln p trace
serves_tasks: Run a coarse grid, then a global optimiser, then a short MCMC, and follow the progress

features.name: Rotation-diagram fitter with clickable line measurements
features.general: Pick lines of one species, measure their fluxes with per-line profile fits, and fit a population diagram (one or two temperatures) to get column density, temperature, extinction and ortho/para ratio
features.specific: Rotation diagram module: choose the input (s3d region, x1d/CSV/FITS, LTE-fit target, flux table), molecule and line list. Run ① Find lines, ② Measure, ③ Fit, ④ MCMC, or Run all (run here without MCMC). The Spectrum tab shows line markers, and clicking a line shows its Gaussian fit. The Lines tab is a table with use/detected flags. The Rotation diagram tab shows ln(N_u/g_u) vs E_u with the fit curves and a summary (logN, T, A_V, OPR).
steps: choose the input and the molecule
press Run all (optionally with MCMC)
inspect the per-line fits and the Lines table
read N, T and OPR on the Rotation diagram tab
serves_tasks: Find, measure and fit lines of one species to get temperature, column and ortho/para ratio
Repeat the diagram for a second species

features.name: Cube map viewer with map-type switch and click-a-pixel spectrum
features.general: Make maps of one line from a spectral cube, switch between map products, and click any pixel to see its spectrum split into components with a fitted profile
features.specific: Cube maps: Open a cube, choose a line and Make maps. Map buttons: continuum, mom 0, masked, extended, velocity, σ(v), mom 1, mom 2, S/N, channel, ratio. Clicking a spaxel marks it and plots continuum-subtracted, point-source, extended and Gaussian-fit traces with S/N. Settings include PSF point-source removal, S/N cuts and MC realisations.
steps: press Open with a cube folder or example
choose a line and press Make maps
switch the map type (mom 0 → velocity)
click a spaxel and read its spectrum and fit
serves_tasks: Open a data cube and make a line-intensity map
Switch to the velocity map and inspect one pixel's spectrum and fit

features.name: Reference line-ID overlay on a spectrum
features.general: Overlay catalogued line positions of a chosen species on a spectrum plot to guide identification
features.specific: Data tab: tick 'line IDs (Banzatti+2025 lists)' and pick a species list (here H2O v=0); triangle markers appear above the spectrum at the listed wavelengths.
steps: open the Data tab
tick line IDs (Banzatti+2025 lists)
pick a species list
read the markers above the spectrum
serves_tasks: Overlay reference line positions on the spectrum
